reason: The crankshaft needs supports on the mechanism base, so the bearing frames look like a sensible first fitting.
expectation: The bearing frames will attach to the base and support the shaft.

effect: The bearing frames are installed, so the base is ready for the shaft.
reason: The shaft bearings should hold the crankshaft in place.
expectation: The crankshaft will be mounted in the bearings.

effect: The crankshaft is mounted, providing a turning shaft for the cam.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The off-centre cam should fit onto the shaft to turn its rotation into an up-and-down motion.
expectation: The cam will attach to the crankshaft.

effect: The cam is mounted, and its changing edge height can drive the follower up and down.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the cam’s purpose clear.
reason: The follower needs a guide to keep its movement aligned with the cam.
expectation: The guide will attach to the mechanism so it can hold the follower rod.

effect: The follower rod must go into the guide before that assembly can be fitted to the mechanism.
reaction: The automatic fitting clarified the assembly order.
reason: The guided follower should fit over the cam so its rod can move with the changing edge height.
expectation: The guided follower will attach to the cam mechanism.

effect: The guided follower is now mounted above the cam, ready for the remaining parts.
reaction: The assembly order is clear now.
reason: The light spring should keep the follower against the cam as it turns.
expectation: The spring will attach to the follower mechanism.

effect: The spring is fitted, and the result suggests comparing its pull with an unhooked run when testing.
reaction: I’m curious how the spring changes the follower’s motion.
reason: The crank handle should let me turn and test the assembled lifter.
expectation: The handle will attach so the crank can be turned.

effect: The comparison showed why the spring matters: it keeps the follower against the cam as the cam falls, making the lift reliable.
reaction: The contrast between the sprung and unhooked runs made the mechanism satisfying to understand.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the spring and testing the lifter were most worthwhile: the comparison showed how the parts work together, not just that they fit.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the bearings and shaft was straightforward but less revealing on its own.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the light follower sometimes hung without the spring’s pull rather than following every fall.

arbitrary.text: The guide had to be combined with the rod before it could be fitted to the mechanism. That order was not obvious to me, though the compatibility feedback clarified it.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how this lifter makes the paper dragon wave; learning why the cam and spring work was worth the short assembly.
